data.content_ref: inline:The target argues that adjudication against SRC_005 is invalid because SRC_005's truthfulness was not independently verified. But the problem standard (§11.3) asks whether the critic-audit flags were correctly *sustained*, not whether the underlying ground-truth artifact was independently validated. An adjudication oracle that stipulates SRC_005 as ground truth is performing exactly the function the problem contemplates: testing critic agreement against the designated verdict. The target conflates 'the oracle cannot test correctness in an absolute epistemic sense' with 'the oracle cannot validly sustain flags.' These are different claims. The flags are about whether critics met the adjudication standard relative to the oracle — which they were tested against. The target's objection is an epistemological grievance about oracle design that the problem did not ask the target to adjudicate, and it does not establish that any specific flag was incorrectly sustained. At most it identifies a hypothetical systematic risk ('critics that dissent... will have higher failure rates'), but it provides no instance of a specific critic whose flag was actually wrongful — making the 'sustained' verdict unimpeached on its own terms.
